info.title: Vern Migration API
info.description: Run Vern as a headless migration engine. Create a migration, upload a customer's files, run the managed agent to generate a preview, then execute and export clean data. See the Migration API guides for concepts and walkthroughs.

get.description: Returns the sources in your account — the systems you migrate customers off of. Sources are addressed by **name** throughout the API; no source ID is exposed.

post.description: Pin the recipe a source reuses as the starting point for future `generate` runs, so one customer's run can't drift the baseline others draw from. Pass `run_id: null` to unpin.

run_id.description: The run whose recipe to pin, or null to unpin.

get.description: Returns the active templates in your account — the importable objects, each with its columns and validation rules. Templates are addressed by **slug**.

200.description: The active templates in your account.

get.description: Fetch one active template by its slug.

post.description: Create a migration workspace for one customer — a workbook with one sheet per template. Requires API-key auth specifically. `external_id` makes creation idempotent: re-sending the same one (with the same source) returns the existing migration with a 200.

name.description: Display name for the migration (e.g. the customer's org name).

source.description: The source name this migration comes from. Optional — omit for a sourceless migration.

external_id.description: Your own identifier for this customer. Alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores. Makes creation idempotent.

templates.description: Template slugs to create sheets from. Omit to use every active template.

201.description: The created migration (200 when an existing migration is returned via external_id idempotency).

post.description: Request one signed upload URL per file, then PUT each file's bytes to its `signed_url`. Files are workbook-level — not mapped to templates.

201.description: One signed upload per requested file.

get.description: List the customer-uploaded files for the migration.

post.description: Start one managed-agent run. `generate` authors the recipe and stops at a preview; `update` edits it per `message`; `clarify` asks a read-only question; `execute` runs the approved preview for real. `generate` opens a preview run and `update`/`clarify`/`execute` resume that same run, so the `run_id` stays stable from preview through execution (a resuming call returns `status: "running"`). Only one run runs at a time per migration (409 with the active run_id otherwise).

message.description: Required for update and clarify — your instruction or question in plain language.

extract_via_api.description: generate only. Controls live API extraction from a connected source: true extracts via the connection (alongside any files), false forces file-only, omitted extracts via API only when no files were uploaded and a connection exists.

value.message: Trim whitespace from every phone number.
Which column did you map Email from?

201.description: The run was accepted. A `generate` is `queued`; a resuming `update`/`clarify`/`execute` is `running`. Poll `poll_url`.

409.description: A run is already in progress (the body carries the active run_id), there is no preview to act on / execute, or the approved preview is no longer resumable (generate a fresh one).

example.error: A run is already in progress for this migration.

get.description: Read a run's state. Every response carries `run_id`, `status`, and `created_at` (plus `answers`, a read-back of your last reply, once you've answered a block); the rest depends on status (`message` while running, `blocked_reason` + `questions`/`credential_request` when blocked, `report` on a completed execute, `error` on failure).

questions.question: Some Status values aren't one of the allowed options. How should I handle them?

credential_request.reason: I need API access to read your contacts.

patch.description: Cancel an in-flight run. The only accepted body is `{ "status": "cancel_requested" }`.

200.description: The run in its updated (canceled) shape.

post.description: Resume a run paused at `blocked` with `blocked_reason: "question"`. Send `answers` as the structured `[{id,value}]` form (one per question) or a free-form string. Only a question-blocked run accepts this (409 otherwise) — a credentials-blocked run is rejected so secrets never enter the agent thread; submit those to `POST .../credentials` instead.

answers.description: Structured answers (one {id,value} per question) or a free-form string.

value.answers: Use the company domain for any missing Email, don't drop the row.

200.description: The run resumed and is running again.

post.description: Resume a run paused at `blocked` with `blocked_reason: "credentials"`. The secrets are stored in a secured vault and never enter the agent thread, the run row, or logs. The target connection is taken from the run's own `credential_request` — a key can only fill the connection the agent asked about. Re-submitting overwrites the stored secret so a rejected credential can be re-entered.

credentials.description: Secret values keyed to the request's schema. Must be a non-empty object.

connection_id.description: Optional guard — if sent, must match the run's credential_request.connection_id.

200.description: Credentials stored; the run resumed and is running again.

409.description: The run isn't awaiting credentials (not blocked, or blocked on a question), connection_id doesn't match, or there's no active credential request yet — retry shortly.

example.error: This run is not awaiting credentials.

get.description: Read the migration's live API source connection, or 404 if none is configured. Never returns secret values — `creds_configured` reports whether credentials are on file.

parameters.name: profile_id
parameters.description: Profile to read; pass the literal `workbook` for the workbook-bound connection.

post.summary: Create or update the source connection
post.description: Attach a live API source to the migration, or update it in place. `credentials` (optional here) go to a secured vault and are never returned; you can also supply them later via Submit credentials.

source_key.description: The connector to attach, lower-cased. Unknown or not-yet-enabled keys return 400.

profile_id.description: Scope to a profile; null binds to the workbook; omit for the default profile.

selected_streams.description: Streams to extract, or null for connector default.

credentials.description: Secret values, vaulted and never returned.

delete.description: Remove the migration's source connection and its stored secrets. Accepts the same optional source_key and profile_id query parameters as GET.

get.description: The latest generated preview — the proposed output, sheet-per-template. 404 until a generate/update run has produced one.
A snapshot of the agent's activity thread across all of the migration's runs, ordered by a stable cross-run sequence. Page forward by passing the previous `last_sequence` as `after`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return only events with sequence greater than this.

get.description: A Server-Sent Events stream of the same thread events. Each message is `event: <type>` + `data: <json>`. The stream ends with `event: done` and closes after ~5 minutes; reconnect with `?after=<last_sequence>` to continue.

Stream one sheet's validated data as a CSV, addressed by `{template_slug}.csv`. The body is streamed (gzip-compressed when the request advertises it) and an `X-Total-Records` header reports the matching count.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The template slug with a .csv suffix, e.g. contacts.csv.

get.description:
The settled record of a migration: what was planned, which files went
in, who approved what, how many rows were written, and whether existing
rows were replaced.

Intended to be fetched once and stored, so you can explain a migration
to your own customer later. It does **not** include the conversation
transcript — that is `/thread` — and it does not include individual row
values.

Available once nothing is in flight, including for migrations that
failed: a run can write rows and then fail, which is exactly when this
matters. While a run is active the endpoint returns `409`.

Pass `?format=md` for the same record as a readable Markdown report.

A migration can be imported again later, so the log always covers every
run to date — a re-fetch is a superset of an earlier one. Use
`generated_at` to tell snapshots apart.

409.description: The migration is still in progress. Body carries the current `status` and `retry_after_seconds`.

503.description: The log could not be assembled. Retryable.

get.description: Durable facts about this customer that the agent honours on every run — "amounts are always USD", "skip internal test records". Distinct from source knowledge, which is about the source software itself.

patch.description:
`knowledge` **replaces** the whole document; an empty string clears it.
The agent rewrites this field the same way, so read, merge, then write.

Pass `if_unmodified_since` with the `updated_at` you read to make that
safe: if it changed underneath you the write is refused with `412`
rather than overwriting.

post.description: Queues an export of one or more destination sheets. One slug produces a CSV, several produce a ZIP. Poll the returned `status_url` for the download link.

schema.description: Provide `slug` or `slugs`; `slugs` wins if both are sent.

status_url.description: Relative path of this job's status endpoint.

404.description: Migration not found, or an unknown template slug.

409.description: A sheet has no exportable data.

502.description: The export worker could not be started. Retryable.

200.description: Job state. `download_url` is set once `status` is `completed`.

get.description: Durable facts about the source software itself — field meanings, enum codes, export quirks. Seeding this means a run does not relearn what you already know.

patch.description: `knowledge` replaces the whole document; an empty string clears it. Use `if_unmodified_since` for safe read-modify-write.

409.description: The source name is ambiguous, or a migration is currently running for this source and holds the knowledge lock.

post.summary: Extract structured data from a document
post.description:
Upload an unstructured file (PDF, Word document, or spreadsheet) and extract it against one or more of your templates. Reducto parses the file, an LLM designs a per-section extraction schema from the templates you name, and the extracted rows come back shaped like those templates.

The whole chain takes 30 seconds to several minutes, so this returns `202` immediately with an `extraction_id`. Poll `GET /extractions/{extraction_id}` until `status` is no longer `processing`.

This endpoint is **stateless**: nothing is written into your workbooks or sheets. The extracted rows are retained for 24 hours and then deleted. Capture them yourself if you need them longer.

file.description: The document to extract. Max 100 MB. Supported: pdf, docx, xlsx, xlsm, xls, xltx, xltm, csv.

templates.description: Template slugs to extract against, as returned by `GET /templates`. Repeat the field or pass one comma-separated value. Omit to use every active template.

instruction.description: Optional free-text guidance for the extraction, e.g. "only the first schedule".

202.description: Accepted. Poll the returned id for the result.

413.description: The file exceeds the 100 MB limit.

502.description: The document could not be submitted to the parsing service.

503.description: Extraction is not available for your data region.

get.summary: Poll an extraction and read its rows
get.description:
Returns `processing` until the extraction settles, then `completed` with the extracted tables, or `failed` with a reason.

Results expire 24 hours after creation, after which this returns `410`.

404.description: No such extraction. Also returned for an extraction belonging to another organisation.

410.description: The extraction has expired and its results were deleted.

503.description: Extraction is not available for your data region.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Your Vern API key. Create one at Settings → API keys.

MigrationId.name: migration_id
MigrationId.description: The migration ID returned by Create a migration.

RunId.name: run_id
RunId.description: The run ID returned by Start a run.

SourceName.name: source
SourceName.description: The source's name, as returned by `GET /sources`. URL-encode names containing spaces.

Unauthorized.description: API key missing, malformed, or revoked.

NotFound.description: The referenced resource isn't in your account.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit hit — back off and retry.

MigrationNotFound.description: No migration with this id in your organisation. Returned rather than `403` so the existence of another organisation's migration is not disclosed.

KnowledgeLocked.description: A migration is currently running and may be rewriting this document.

KnowledgeStale.description: The document changed after the `if_unmodified_since` you supplied. The body carries the current `updated_at`; re-read, merge, and retry.

SourceNotFound.description: No source with this name in your organisation.

AmbiguousSource.description: More than one source shares this name. Rename one so the reference is unambiguous.

strictRule.description: Regex the value must match (when desiredRule is strict).

id.description: The migration ID — pass it to every later call.

inserted.description: Total rows imported across all sheets.

invalidCellCount.description: Rows that still carry at least one invalid cell.

coverage.description: Optional per-column fill/distinct profile of sources vs. outputs.

Run.description: A run's polled state. Fields beyond run_id/status/created_at depend on status.

answers.description: A read-back of your last reply, present once you've answered a block.

blocked_reason.description: Present when blocked — which kind of block it is.

questions.description: Present when blocked for a question.

CredentialRequest.description: Present when a run is blocked for credentials. Describes the live source needing secrets — render a form from `schema` and POST to .../credentials. Carries no secret values.

connection_id.description: The source connection the secrets belong to.

reason.description: Why the agent needs access. May be absent.

guidance.description: Optional help — { summary?, steps?, links? } — for where to find the credentials.

schema.description: The fields to collect, keyed by name.

SourceConnection.description: A migration's live API source connection. Never includes secret values; `creds_configured` reports whether credentials are stored.

name.description: Connector display name; falls back to source_key.

last_snapshot.description: Metadata about the most recent extraction.

rows.description: Rows as a grid, header row first.

sequence.description: Stable cross-run ordinal; use as the next `after`.

type.description: message | thinking | status | tool_call | tool_result | task | request_input | prepared | preview | completed | error.

MigrationStatus.description:
- `awaiting_files` — no files uploaded and no source connection
- `ready` — inputs present, no plan yet
- `awaiting_approval` — a preview is waiting to be executed
- `completed` — an import has run successfully

knowledge.description: Replaces the whole document. Empty string clears it.

if_unmodified_since.description: The `updated_at` you last read. Supply it to get `412` instead of silently overwriting a concurrent change.

download_url.description: A time-limited link, present once the job is complete.

templates.description: The template slugs this extraction runs against.

expires_at.description: After this, the result is deleted and GET returns 410.

row_count.description: Total rows across all tables. Present when `completed`.

started_by.description: Null when the run was started through this API.

replaced_existing_data.description: True when this run emptied its destination sheets before writing — it replaced the previous import rather than adding to it.

name.description: The section this table came from, when the extraction identified one. Null for an unnamed table.

rows.description: One object per row, keyed by header.

ordinal.description: 1-based position of this table within the document.

pages.description: Source pages this table was drawn from, when known.
